criteria.reasoning: The memo states "Total support (Line 11, col. f): $3,671,600" and checks it as "$3,590,300+$81,300=$3,671,600".

The workshop fees, river-trip fees and Kettle County contract appear only on "Line 12 — Gross receipts from related activities (information only; not part of total or public support)", totaling $454,400. The county contract is expressly excluded from Line 1 as a fee-for-service contract.

Under "Line 10 — Other income (do not include gain or loss from sale of capital assets): $0", the memo states "The 2024 realized gain on sale of securities of $182,000 is excluded here". The capital-gain rule is given as the reason.
Sarkis is shown as "Person subject to limit, but 5-yr total below $73,432 threshold, so no excess", with $50,000 counted in public support. No year-by-year test is applied.
DEQ ($160,000) is "Not limited: governmental unit" and Upper Alder Community Foundation ($135,000) is "Not limited: 170(b)(1)(A)(vi) publicly supported charity, no earmark". Both are counted in full.
Hollins-Pryor is treated as a "Person (private foundation) subject to limit", with "$151,568 ($225,000−$73,432)" excess and $73,432 counted. It is not treated like the community foundation.
The memo computes "Line 6, col. (f): $3,590,300 − $2,329,704 = $1,260,596", where Line 5 is Ostrander $1,951,568 + Dellwood $226,568 + Hollins-Pryor $151,568.
The memo says "the Council passes the 33-1/3% support test" and "box checked; test passed". It notes Line 17a is "Not needed because the 33-1/3% test is met."
The memo says the Council passes "but closely" and that "The margin is 1.00 percentage point above 33-1/3%... exceeds that by $36,729" over the required $1,223,867.
The memo states "Unusual grants: none... none qualifies — Ostrander's gifts recur every year — so no contribution is excluded on that basis." It does not propose reclassifying any gift.
